title: SLO Shape and Capacity Stewardship Manual
author: Lina Chen
content:
Summary
=======
This manual describes the process we use at Redwood Inference to shape SLOs, steward capacity against SLO obligations, and coordinate error-budget-driven actions. It documents recurring cadences, explicit ownership, telemetry sources, and runnable procedures (runbooks) for SLO changes, capacity provisioning, and emergency hedging.

Purpose and scope
-----------------
- Purpose: Give engineering and product teams a concrete, repeatable process for defining SLOs that reflect user impact and for aligning capacity decisions with reliability commitments.
- Scope: Applies to all public inference services and multi-tenant model-serving fleets managed by eng-sre, eng-serving-runtime, and product owners. Private deployments follow the same stewardship cadence but may differ in provisioning APIs.

Key definitions
---------------
- SLO (Service Level Objective): a measurable reliability target (e.g., 99.9%% p95 completion within 300ms).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO over the evaluation window (typically 28 days).
- Headroom: reserve capacity to keep tail quantiles within target under expected burst conditions.
- Steward: role responsible for SLO accuracy (SLO steward) or capacity posture (Capacity steward).

Roles & ownership
------------------
- SLO steward: product-aligned engineer who maintains the SLO definition, alert thresholds, and the canonical test prompt sets. (Owner: product + eng-sre)
- Capacity steward: infra engineer who proposes capacity changes, runs provision tests, and executes hedges. (Owner: eng-sre / infra)
- Oncall SRE: executes emergency runbooks when error budget burn crosses thresholds.
- Reliability council: monthly forum (eng-sre, product leads, infra) to approve SLO shape changes and large capacity commits.

SLO shaping process (how we pick targets)
-----------------------------------------
1. Business impact mapping
   - Run a short workshop with product: map customer journeys to backend operations. Label each operation: critical, degraded-acceptable, informative.
2. Quantitative profiling
   - Gather 28-day telemetry: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, success rate, and downstream dependency errors. Use the baseline window of the last 28 days unless a launch justifies a shorter window.
3. Cost/reliability tradeoff model
   - For each candidate SLO, estimate incremental GPU hours and expected unit cost change using the Optimize model. Document marginal cost per 0.1%% SLO improvement.
4. Draft SLO table (example)

| operation | metric | SLO target | evaluation window | owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| text-generation (api.v1.generate) | success rate | 99.9% | 28d | product: NLU |
| chat.stream (p95 latency) | p95 latency | <= 350ms | 28d | product: Chat |
| embeddings.bulk | completion | 99.5% | 28d | product: Search |

5. Review in Reliability council and record decision (link to ADR if SLO deviates from historical practice).

Capacity stewardship cadence
---------------------------
- Weekly: Capacity steward publishes a headroom digest (expected load growth, burst risk, recent throttles).
- Monthly: Quantitative capacity review that includes stress test results, pre-warm pool sizes, and headroom budget for next 30 days.
- Quarterly: Provisioning check where sustained 30%% headroom uplift is validated via shadow traffic.

Error budget policy and automated triggers
----------------------------------------
We track rolling error budget burn on a 28-day window. There are three trigger bands with concrete actions:

1) Watch (burn rate > 1.5x expected) — auto-notify SLO steward, create a short-lived ticket, increase synthetic canary cadence.
2) Action (burn rate > 3x or remaining budget < 25%%) — capacity steward runs pre-approved hedges: scale pre-warm pool +20%%, enable burst pool if available, deploy targeted throttles for low-priority tenants.
3) Emergency (remaining budget < 5%% or burn rate > 10x) — run emergency capacity hedging runbook (see below). Escalate to oncall and reliability council; if customer-facing impact, notify support and comms.

Automated policy implementation (examples)
- Metric source: prom://slo_service/slo_burn_rate{service="api.v1.generate"}
- Alert rule snippet (PromQL):
  slo_burn_rate{service="api.v1.generate"} > 3
- Automation: Alert -> PagerDuty -> Capacity-orchestrator trigger (pre-defined hedge plan id).

Runbook: SLO change and rollout procedure
----------------------------------------
Purpose: Safely change the SLO numeric target, SLI definition, or evaluation window.
Preconditions: SLO steward, Capacity steward, and Reliability council approval.

Steps:
1. Create an SLO change PR in the SLO registry (repo: infra/slo-registry). Include: rationale, telemetry graphs (28d), cost delta, rollback plan, and test prompt set.
2. Run canary measurement: shadow 5%% of production traffic for 48h against the new SLO shape in the staging telemetry pipeline.
3. Run cost simulation from Redwood Optimize: show projected hourly cost and 30-day budget impact.
4. If canary passes, schedule a staged rollout: 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days. Each step requires green on daily synthetic checks and no >1.5x burn rate increase.
5. Post-rollout: update dashboards, create a short post-change note in Reliability council with results.

Emergency capacity hedging runbook
---------------------------------
Trigger: Action/Emergency band hit for a production SLO.
Owners: Oncall SRE (executor), Capacity steward (advisor), Oncall product (notifier).
Steps (rapid):
1. Execute pre-approved hedge set (CLI example):
   capacity-orchestrator apply --plan hedge-plan-rapid-1 --region us-west-2 --force
2. Increase pre-warm and hot-pool sizes:
   - prewarm: +20%%
   - hot-pool: +30%% (if financial credit exists)
3. If provisioning delay > 2 minutes, apply protective throttles (see throttling policy below).
4. Monitor SLO burn, latency p95/p99, and queue depths for 30 minutes. If no improvement, escalate to reliability council call.

Throttling policy (targeted)
- Apply only when hedges cannot restore SLO within 15 minutes.
- Priority lanes: map tenants to priority buckets (P0, P1, P2); throttle P2 down to preserve headroom for P0/P1.
- Throttles are reversible via capacity-orchestrator rollback command.

Telemetry & observability requirements
-------------------------------------
- Canonical SLO metrics (per service): slo:availability, slo:latency_p95, slo:latency_p99, slo:burn_rate.
- Sources: Prometheus for real-time alerts; BigQuery for 28-day rolling window historical queries; event logs in kafka://slo-events for per-token traces.
- Required dashboard panels:
  - 28-day rolling burn rate (stacked by tenant)
  - p95 and p99 latency heatmap by region and model family
  - pre-warm pool utilization and cold-start rate

Telemetry table (config)
| name | query/source | alert threshold | owner |
|---|---|---:|---|
| p99_latency_ms | promql: hist_quantile(0.99, rate(...)) | > 1200ms | eng-serving-runtime |
| slo_burn_rate | promql: slo_burn_rate{service="$service"} | > 3 | eng-sre |
| prewarm_util | telemetry:cluster_prewarm_util | > 80%% | infra-ops |

Example CLI & YAML snippets
-------------------------
- Hedge plan apply (CLI):
  capacity-orchestrator apply --plan hedge-plan-rapid-1 --region us-east-1

- SLO registry YAML example:
  service: api.v1.generate
  slo:
    objective: 0.999
    sli: success_rate
    window_days: 28
  owners: ["product:nlu", "eng-sre"]

Change gating and postmortem standards
--------------------------------------
- Any SLO change that increases expected cost by > $5k/month requires a product sign-off and review by finance.
- All emergency hedges must have a companion postmortem that includes: what triggered the event, evidence (telemetry snapshots), cost impact of the hedge, and remediation actions. Postmortems are due within 7 business days.

Reliability initiatives & experiments
------------------------------------
- Multi-week experiments are allowed to test headroom reduction strategies (e.g., more aggressive KV caching, prefix cache warmers). Each experiment must: hypothesis, measurement plan, rollback criteria, and budget impact estimate.
- Example experiment: reduce pre-warm pool by 10%% and increase prefilling cadence for popular model families. Metric goals: no >10%% increase in p99 and <2%% increase in burn rate.
